Quirk Registration and Counseling.text: Every Quirk in Japan is registered. When a child manifests a power, usually around age four, the family takes them to a doctor or a licensed Quirk counselor. The counselor examines the Quirk, gives it a working name and a description, notes its type, triggers and risks, and files it with the national registry. Children whose Quirk has not appeared by the usual age get a medical check, and the finding is recorded the same way. Counseling continues wherever a Quirk is dangerous to the child or to others: counselors teach control, safe habits and the law, and they advise parents and schools. Good counseling helps a child live with their power without shame; rigid counseling teaches a child to hide what they are, and some people resent it for life. Registry records follow a person into adulthood. A registered Quirk appears in school and hospital files, and employers may ask about it where safety depends on it. A Quirk that grows, changes or turns out to work differently than first thought should be updated, and updates for late developers are routine paperwork. The police and the Hero Public Safety Commission can consult the registry in an investigation, which is one reason Quirk criminals are often identified quickly. A private citizen cannot look up a stranger's Quirk, and the registry holds only what was reported to it.
